subject: error-handling

note: The fork arm ran statically over the tree; the detector arm could not. All 3 construction sites answer NO to the separating question (can a user reach this through a documented interface with values it accepts?), so declaration was right, caller is the bug, and there is nothing to reclassify. The tree had ALREADY taken the other branch deliberately: ErrorCode::Unsupported was split out of Internal with a comment saying a permanent capability gap must not read as a transient outage. Same reasoning again in the parsing direction at e7fcc7c, which replaced unwrap_or_default() in parse_enum and drew the fork per vocabulary — Provider::Unknown and Operation::Other are deliberate quarantine variants, status and redaction have no such member. not-better is correct and it amended the technique: a taxonomy already split deliberately gives the fork nothing to find. THE DETECTOR HALF IS GENUINELY ABSENT AND CHEAP — the only assertions naming the class are two unit tests of the error type itself; zero tests assert it never fires across the suite, and the expensive prerequisite (a stable wire string with a test pinning it) is already built.
return_condition: build a suite-wide sweep of integration-test responses for the "internal" wire string and re-run; until that instrument exists the detector claim is asserted and unmeasured
